text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bell to cut 2,200 more jobs: Phone giant tells employees competitive pressure demands layoffs within three months
Salmon war declared by B.C.: Alaskan catch angers Clark
Milgaard expects DNA result today: Blood of serial rapist available for testing if man who served time is cleared
Mir tumbles in dark as cable unplugged: Crew of ill-fated station use flashlights
Mounting labor unrest alarms China's leaders: Disgruntled workers angry over shutdown of state factories
Toronto's destitute wear out welcome: Downtown middle-class residents fed up with addicts, prostitutes want to evict drop-in social agencies from their streets.
UGG, Archer-Daniels unite: Unied Grain Growers shareholders approve $133 million alliance with U.S. food giant
Kmart Canada eyes closing up to 20 stores: Weakest outlets placed on review list
Sears'profit propels stock: Hits 52-week high based on best second quarter in 8 years
B.C. developers applaud withdrawal of labor code bill: Business backlash forces about-face.
CIBC in talks to acquire Canada Trust: Price would be at least $4.8 billion and a deal would create the country's biggest bank
